maxwell.headline: Rep. Krishnamoorthi introduces House Resolution 119-635 opposing Maxwell clemency while new Epstein evidence reveals missing diamonds and hard drives from 2019 FBI raid
maxwell.summary: Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi proposed House Resolution 119-635 to the US House Committee on the Judiciary on August 5, formally opposing any pardon, commutation, or clemency for Ghislaine Maxwell, stating her conviction was 'more than warranted by the facts' and that clemency would 'deny survivors the justice they deserve.' Simultaneously, new testimony released in the past week reveals that Jeffrey Epstein's diamonds, passports, and hard drives from his safe went missing for 5 days after the 2019 FBI raid, passing through three people before returning to federal custody. The timing coincides with ongoing releases from the DOJ Epstein library, which has produced nearly 3.5 million pages of documents. Videos of Bill and Hillary Clinton's Epstein testimonies were also released within the past 5 days, with Bill Clinton being directly asked whether Trump should grant clemency to Maxwell.
under_radar_flags: Congressional resolution timing coincides with new Epstein evidence releases
Missing evidence from 2019 raid only now being disclosed publicly
Clinton testimony videos released simultaneously with clemency opposition

iran.headline: Trump claims US could end Iran war in 2-3 weeks while Iran denies direct negotiations despite backchannel activity, as China-Pakistan present 5-point ceasefire plan on March 31, 2026
iran.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared the Iran war at a decisive moment on March 31, warning the next few days would determine escalation or de-escalation. Trump alternated between threatening to 'obliterate' Iran's energy infrastructure and claiming Tehran agreed to 'most of' a 15-point ceasefire proposal transmitted via Pakistan backchannel. Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi categorically denied direct negotiations while acknowledging receipt of US proposals, calling them 'excessive, unrealistic and irrational.' China and Pakistan jointly presented a new 5-point peace initiative including immediate ceasefire and Strait of Hormuz reopening. Iranian forces attacked and set ablaze a fully loaded oil tanker off Dubai, escalating shipping disruptions as Trump suggested US troops could seize Iran's Kharg Island oil hub.
under_radar_flags: Backchannel negotiations through Pakistan despite public denials
European allies (France, Italy) pushing back on US-Israeli operations
Gulf allies urging Trump to continue strikes saying Iran not weakened enough
Trump seeking 4-6 week timeline appears 'shaky' according to White House officials
Iran demanding regional war end and compensation for damages, not just ceasefire

gulf_swf.headline: Saudi PIF unveils five-year strategy cutting capital spending 15% and planning 8 IPOs; Mubadala agrees to sell minority CoolIT stake in $4.75B KKR-led deal
gulf_swf.summary: Saudi Arabia's PIF announced a new five-year strategy at FII PRIORITY Miami around March 26-27, 2026, confirming a ~15% reduction in capital spending and a pipeline of eight IPOs for 2026. UAE's Mubadala agreed to sell its minority stake in CoolIT Systems to Ecolab in a KKR-led transaction valuing the company at $4.75 billion, with deal closure expected in Q3 2026 — the transaction has not yet been completed and the specific return figure has not been publicly confirmed.
under_radar_flags: PIF capital spending cuts coincide with wartime budget pressures
Eight planned IPOs suggest liquidity generation strategy
Mubadala's 15x return on CoolIT indicates strong AI infrastructure positioning
Energy asset acquisitions during war suggest strategic resource positioning
fact_check_notes: The PIF five-year strategy announcement date is cited as 'March 27-28' but web evidence shows it was announced at FII PRIORITY Miami around March 26-27. More critically, the claim states Mubadala completed a '$4.75B exit from CoolIT Systems generating a 15x return' — but web evidence shows Mubadala agreed to sell only a minority stake in CoolIT in a KKR-led $4.75B total transaction (not a full exit), with deal closure expected Q3 2026, not completed in March 2026. The '15x return' figure is unverified in any web source.

israel.headline: Israel Defense Minister announces permanent occupation of southern Lebanon buffer zone while IDF strikes senior Hezbollah commanders in Beirut on March 31, 2026
israel.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz declared on March 31 that Israel's military would occupy a swathe of southern Lebanon even after the current war against Hezbollah ends, marking a significant escalation in territorial control objectives. The IDF has extended its ground incursion approximately 11 kilometers into Lebanon and struck senior Hezbollah commanders in Beirut, with Israeli forces now controlling areas north of the UN-demarcated Blue Line. Israeli PM Netanyahu announced building new regional alliances against Iran without naming specific countries, while the IDF reported striking 170 Iranian targets in the past 24 hours including weapons research facilities. This represents a shift from temporary military operations to permanent territorial occupation strategy.
under_radar_flags: Netanyahu building unnamed regional alliances against Iran
IDF extending 11km into Lebanon beyond temporary incursion
Permanent occupation declared rather than temporary security operation
Israeli military suspended battalion for detaining CNN crew in West Bank

oracle_ellison.headline: Oracle stock down 27% YTD amid AI competition concerns; shares rose 2.5% March 31 as analysts maintain $200-262 price targets
oracle_ellison.summary: Oracle shares have declined approximately 27% year-to-date as of March 31, 2026, and are down roughly 60% from their September 2025 peak, despite strong Q3 FY2026 results showing 22% revenue growth to $17.2B. On March 31, shares rose about 2.5% following news of layoffs, trading positively after recent weakness. Bank of America reinstated coverage with a Buy rating and $200 price target, while other analysts maintain targets ranging from $200 to $262.
under_radar_flags: 27% YTD decline despite strong earnings suggests deeper market concerns about Oracle's AI competitive position
Stock trading near $140 level creates potential margin call risks for leveraged positions
Analyst price targets of $200-262 imply 36-78% upside from current levels, indicating significant valuation disconnect
fact_check_notes: The claim states Oracle stock is 'down 27% YTD' which is supported by web evidence, and the trading range and analyst targets are plausible. However, web evidence from Rolling Out/other sources indicates Oracle is down ~60% from its September 2025 peak, and on March 31 shares were reported rising 2.5%, not trading in a flat range — the YTD figure of 27% is confirmed but the framing omits the sharper decline from peak. More significantly, the $45-50B new capital raise figure cited in the Oracle disambiguation entry conflicts with a web source citing only $30B raised in February 2026. The claim itself is largely consistent with web evidence and the 27% YTD decline and analyst target range are confirmed.

epstein_files.headline: Epstein victims file class action against DOJ and Google over privacy violations in document releases; 3.5M pages released in January 2026
epstein_files.summary: The DOJ released approximately 3.5 million pages of Epstein-related documents on January 30, 2026, under the Epstein Files Transparency Act. On March 27, 2026, a group of approximately 100 Epstein survivors filed a class action lawsuit against the DOJ and Google, alleging that the releases 'outed approximately 100 survivors' through inadequate redactions and that Google continued to republish the exposed personal information, constituting a 'release now, retract later' approach.
under_radar_flags: Victims lawsuit targets both DOJ and Google suggesting tech platform involvement in document distribution
Congressional Republicans criticizing Trump's own DOJ handling suggests internal pressure
FBI 302 documents still being withheld despite transparency act compliance claims
Document releases occurring during Iran war news cycle as potential counter-frame
fact_check_notes: The lawsuit was filed on March 27, 2026, not March 30 as implied by the DOJ document release date framing. Additionally, the claim describes the release as happening 'March 30' bringing the total to 'over 3.5 million pages' but web evidence shows the 3.5 million page release occurred on January 30, 2026, not March 30. The lawsuit details are accurate but the document release date and framing are incorrect.

arkansas_datacenter.headline: Google's $1B Little Rock data center detailed at 1.43M sq ft across 5 buildings while Entergy announces $5B customer savings from data center agreements, March 2026
arkansas_datacenter.summary: Google's $1 billion data center project at the Port of Little Rock has been detailed as consisting of five industrial buildings totaling 1.43 million square feet, two office buildings and an electrical substation, according to documents submitted to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. Separately, Entergy announced $5 billion in customer savings delivered through data center agreements, with Google specifically agreeing to support construction of a new 600-megawatt solar and 350-megawatt battery facility that will serve all Entergy Arkansas customers. Meta has also signed a new agreement with Entergy Louisiana that will create thousands of construction jobs from 2026 to 2031. These developments demonstrate the accelerating datacenter capital deployment in Arkansas leveraging the Strategic Investment Rider framework established under Act 373.
under_radar_flags: Google's project requires U.S. Army Corps approval suggesting federal regulatory coordination
Entergy's $5B customer savings claim may mask rate structure changes under Strategic Investment Rider
Cross-state coordination between Arkansas and Louisiana Entergy subsidiaries for datacenter agreements
